title: String Compression
statement:
Shorten a string by writing each run of the same letter once, followed by how long the run is.

The input is one line of lowercase letters, with at least one letter. A run is a group of the same letter in a row. Write each run as its letter followed by its length, and leave the length out when the run is a single letter, so `aaabcc` becomes `a3bc2`. A run can be 10 letters or longer, and then its length has more than one digit. When a letter shows up again after a different one, it starts a new run. Print the result.

Input:

```text
aaabcc
```

Expected output:

```text
a3bc2
```
hints: Keep an index at the start of the current run, and move a second index forward while the letter stays the same. The run's length is the distance between the two.

Turn the length into text with your language's call for that (`str` in Python, `String` or a template string in JavaScript and TypeScript, `std::to_string` in C++, `strconv.Itoa` in Go). Java's `StringBuilder.append` takes the number as it is.

Adding to a string again and again can copy the whole string each time. Collect the pieces and join them once (a list and `"".join` in Python, an array and `join` in JavaScript and TypeScript), or use a builder made for it (`StringBuilder` in Java, `strings.Builder` in Go). In C++, `+=` on a `std::string` grows it in place.
